eyebrow: Step 1 — a sudo user, verified before anything else
code:
$ sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash deploy
$ sudo usermod -aG sudo deploy

$ su - deploy
$ sudo whoami
[sudo] password for deploy:
root
caption: Confirm sudo whoami returns root before relying on this account for anything

eyebrow: Step 2 — generate, install, and PROVE a key works
code:
$ ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "deploy@app-02"
$ ssh-copy-id deploy@app-02
Number of key(s) added: 1

$ ssh deploy@app-02
Welcome to Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
deploy@app-02:~$
caption: Logged in with no password prompt — keep this session open for the next step

eyebrow: Step 3 — lock down sshd, test before restarting
code:
# /etc/ssh/sshd_config
PermitRootLogin no
PasswordAuthentication no

$ sudo sshd -t
$ sudo systemctl restart ssh
$ sudo sshd -T | grep -iE "permitrootlogin|passwordauth"
permitrootlogin no
passwordauthentication no
caption: sshd -t catches a syntax error before it locks you out — never skip it

eyebrow: Steps 4–6 — firewall, service, cron, in order
code:
$ sudo ufw allow OpenSSH && sudo ufw enable
Firewall is active and enabled on system startup

$ sudo systemctl enable --now northbridge-tool
$ sudo crontab -u deploy -l
0 2 * * * /opt/northbridge/bin/nightly-cleanup.sh >> /var/log/northbridge/nightly-cleanup.log 2>&1
caption: Allow SSH before enabling ufw, or the firewall drops your own connection
